Message', S3 (and the live table) has THREE columns H8-1..H8-3, and nothing in the paper or supplements ties any column to any statement. The four S1 statements, in print order: (1) "Phrased in clear language, avoiding obscure codes. Example of obscure code: “system crashed, error code 147.’’" (2) "Precise, not vague or general. Example of general comment: “Cannot open document.”" (3) "The system provides constructive messages when error happens." (4) "The system provides polite messages when errors occur. Examples of impolite message: “illegal user action,” “job aborted,” “system was crashed,” “fatal error,” etc.". WHAT WAS CHECKED. (a) S1 layout, page 5 rendered: the four statements are ordinary, visually identical item rows, each with its own Advantage/Disadvantage cells and five checkboxes; none is a heading, sub-heading, example line or duplicate. (b) Family-wide count: S1 prints 6/4/3/4/7/4/3/4/4/3/4/3/2/3 statements for H1..H14 = 54; S3 has 53 heuristic columns; H8 is the only block that disagrees. (d) Article: no statement that an H8 item was removed; Methods only says the instrument was based on Zhang et al. and Davis et al. 'with modifications to match the research topic and eliminate irrelevant items' (generic, names no item). Table 3 reports heuristic-level statistics only (H8 factor loading 0.84, item-total r 0.863); no per-item statistic for any heuristic. (e) Crossref: no correction or update notice. (f) A web search for another report of this data with item-level H8 results found none (not exhaustive). DATA EVIDENCE (S3 xlsx; live per-item means via item_stats.R equal the xlsx: 4.31/3.66/4.46). Level counts 1..5: H8-1 0/0/14/42/45 (mean 4.307), H8-2 2/10/25/47/17 (3.663), H8-3 0/2/10/29/60 (4.455). The three columns ARE the analysed H8 block: the heuristic mean of H8-1..H8-3 reproduces the whole System Support profile of Table 3/4 (item-total r H7 0.749, H8 0.863, H9 0.768, H11 0.856, H12 0.806, alpha 0.855, mean 4.031; max deviation 0.00045); dropping any one column misses by 0.031 (drop H8-3; H8 r 0.86) / 0.045 (drop H8-1) / 0.077 (drop H8-2); a single column alone misses by 0.095-0.14. Adding ANY other S3 heuristic column as a putative fourth H8 item never reproduces (best: H5-1, max dev 0.0092; 0 of 50 within 0.0015), so the published analysis used exactly three H8 responses -- the missing statement is absent from the analysis, not just from the S3 export. What the data cannot say: which S1 statement lacks data. Every published statistic is a function of the H8 mean, which is blind to which printed statement each column answers. Circumstantial only, not usable: H8-1 is identical to H6-1 in 97/101 rows (r 0.93) and to H12-1 'Use standard meanings of words.' and H12-2 'Specialized language for specialized groups.' in 95/101 (r 0.94/0.91), which fits statement 1 (clear language) but equally fits the S3 file-wide pattern of content-unrelated identical-answer clusters (H6-1 'Information that can be directly perceived...' is unrelated); H8-2 is identical to H9-4 91/101 (r 0.85), H9-2 88/101, H11-4 88/101 (all error-prevention items), which fits any of statements 2-4 about errors; H8-3 has no close partner (max 66/101 identical, max r 0.54 with H12-3 'User can define aliases.'). Within-block: H8-1~H8-2 37/101 (r 0.19), H8-1~H8-3 59/101 (r 0.43), H8-2~H8-3 36/101 (r 0.36). H8-2's low mean (3.66 vs 4.31/4.46) is not tied to any statement by anything published. DECISION: no item-level tie can be established. Assigning H8-1..H8-3 to S1 statements 1-3 by print order would assume the fourth statement is the one without data, which nothing supports over the three alternatives (4 choices of the missing statement x 6 orders = 24 mappings, all equally consistent with every published number). Unlike the 12 shipped siblings, where S1 block size = S3 column count so the shipped text SET is right and only within-block order is open, here the set itself is unknown: one printed statement corresponds to no data.
